prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He did not question the validation (A) / of the technical parameters because of he trusted (B) / the core competency of the senior research head. (C) / No Error (D)
options: He did not question the validation
of the technical parameters because of he trusted
the core competency of the senior research head.
explanation: 'Because of' is a preposition and cannot introduce a clause with a subject and verb. Part (B) should use the conjunction 'because he trusted'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My sister and I / work very hard / nevertheless my brother does not do / any task assigned to him.
options: nevertheless my brother does not do
explanation: 'Nevertheless' is a conjunctive adverb and cannot join the clauses here; a contrast conjunction like 'but' or 'whereas' is needed.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Seldom had the tribunal entertained an appeal (1)/ so lacking in substance, nor so plainly designed (2)/ to invite publicity rather than justice. (3)/ No error (4)/
explanation: The two modifiers of 'appeal' should be joined by 'or' ('so lacking in substance, or so plainly designed'); 'nor' is incorrect as no second negative clause follows.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: He lived close to / the train station, / yet travelled by bus.
explanation: 'Lived close to the train station' and the contrast marker 'yet travelled by bus' are both idiomatic and grammatically correct, so the sentence has no error.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This dog seems / to be very ferocious, / otherwise, / it is harmless.
explanation: The sense is contrast, not alternative consequence, so 'otherwise' should be 'but'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: You must be careful about what you say as you meet her.
explanation: The clause states a point of time, so the time conjunction 'when' is needed instead of 'as'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: As such you need any money, just write to me.
explanation: The clause states a condition, so 'As such you' should be 'If you' (or 'In case you').

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She will come to work though it doesn’t rain tomorrow.
explanation: The intended concessive-conditional meaning needs 'even if it rains tomorrow'; 'though it doesn't rain' contradicts the sense.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The farmers are using / HYV seeds / so then they can get / a better yield.
explanation: A clause of purpose requires the conjunction 'so that', not 'so then'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Professor Gupta is an authority / on income tax because / he cannot exercise / any authority over his family.
explanation: The two clauses express contrast, not cause, so 'because' should be replaced by 'although/though'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. Do not let the opportunity slip away and you will repent. /No error
explanation: After a negative imperative expressing a warning, 'or' is required to show the consequence — 'or you will repent'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Let us not neglect important aspects of life although pursue momentary pleasures.
explanation: 'While pursuing' correctly expresses simultaneous action; 'although' wrongly introduces contrast with a non-clause.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: The Ghats in Benaras were very crowded but we were able to watch the Ganga aarti clearly.
explanation: The contrast between the crowded Ghats and being able to watch clearly is correctly shown by 'but we were'; no change is needed.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: I couldn’t sleep in case of being very tired.
explanation: The sense is concession (couldn't sleep despite tiredness), and only 'in spite of' can be followed by the gerund 'being'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement’. I will accept the responsibility while a time comes.
explanation: A specific future point requires 'when the time comes'; 'while' indicates duration and 'a time' is indefinite.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement’. She was smiling but looking pleased about something.
explanation: There is no contrast between smiling and looking pleased, so the additive 'and looked' is appropriate and keeps the verbs parallel.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. We shall rehearse thrice before the final performance at least we make errors in the dialogues.
explanation: 'Lest' means 'for fear that / so that ... not', which correctly expresses the purpose of rehearsing to avoid errors.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: Because she didn’t love him, she had to marry him.
explanation: The two clauses express contrast, not cause, so the concessive conjunction 'Although' is needed.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: The train was delayed in order to an accident.
explanation: 'Owing to' is the correct prepositional phrase before the noun 'an accident'; 'in order to' expresses purpose, not cause.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: She could not attend my brother’s marriage in spite of her illness.
explanation: Illness is the reason for her absence, not a concession, so 'because of' is required instead of 'in spite of'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.
sentence: Inspite mother’s milk is vital to a child’s health, a number of FMCG companies wrongly advertise artificially prepared infant formulas as being the best for the child.
explanation: The clause needs a subordinating conjunction, not the preposition 'Inspite/Despite', because a full clause ('mother's milk is vital') follows; 'Though' correctly expresses the contrast.

prompt: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In
sentence: case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. October has four consecutive holidays but we are planning a trip to Andaman Islands
explanation: The four holidays are the cause and the trip is the result, so the conjunction of result 'so' is needed instead of the contrastive 'but'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: An awkward neither grammatically accurate sentence is the result of centre implanting.
explanation: The two adjectives express contrast (awkward yet grammatical), so the contrastive conjunction 'but' is required, not 'neither'.

prompt: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In
sentence: case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. We should always wash our hands during having food.
explanation: Hands are washed prior to eating, so 'before having food' is the logical connector; 'during' is also ungrammatical before a gerund clause here.
